[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) & Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD) in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This technical tutorial explores Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) and Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD) from the perspective of a manual testing professional. While these methodologies heavily emphasize automation, manual testers play a crucial role in defining, reviewing, and executing acceptance criteria and behavior scenarios."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding ATDD and BDD Core Concepts"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ATDD (Acceptance Test-Driven Development): Focuses on collaborating with customers, developers, and testers to define precise acceptance criteria before development begins. It answers the question: Are we building the right thing?"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BDD (Behavior-Driven Development): An evolution of ATDD that focuses on the behavioral aspects of user stories using a common, human-readable language. It bridges the communication gap between business stakeholders and technical teams."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. The Role of Manual Testers in BDD/ATDD"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"In a BDD/ATDD workflow, manual testers act as facilitators during 'Three Amigos' sessions (Business Analyst, Developer, and Tester). Testers contribute by identifying edge cases, clarifying ambiguous business rules, and writing scenarios in Gherkin syntax."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Writing Gherkin Syntax Scenarios"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"BDD uses the Given-When-Then structure (Gherkin language) to define test scenarios clearly and unambiguously."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"Feature: User Authentication

  Scenario: Successful login with valid credentials
    Given the user is on the login page
    When the user enters valid username "john_doe" and password "Secret123"
    And clicks the login button
    Then the user should be redirected to the dashboard page"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Step-by-Step Manual Testing Workflow for ATDD"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Requirement Analysis - Review user stories alongside stakeholders to extract acceptance criteria."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Acceptance Test Creation - Draft manual test cases directly mapped from the ATDD acceptance criteria."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 3: Exploratory & Execution Phase - Execute the manual scenarios against the newly built feature to validate expected behaviors."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 4: Feedback Loop - Report discrepancies and collaborate with developers to refine future behavior definitions."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Adopting BDD and ATDD principles transforms manual testers from reactive bug finders into proactive quality advocates. By focusing on behavior and acceptance criteria early in the lifecycle, manual testers ensure high alignment between business goals and delivered software."}]
